reading.body:
A point tagged as a data center in Siena, Italy is an accounting firm, and the tag is best read as a mapping error.

The name carries the answer. "Accounting" in the business name identifies a bookkeeping practice serving local clients, not a hosting or colocation business. An accounting office runs its own computers and may keep client financial records on a server, but that is a different function from a commercial data center. The telecom=data_center tag most plausibly reflects the firm's own small server room or network closet.

This matters for AI because facility counts are used to estimate available compute. A mislabeled office adds a site that supplies no capacity, and errors of this kind inflate the denominator without adding megawatts. The record lists zero megawatts, which is consistent with an office rather than a powered facility.

What the data does not cover is how often this happens. It is one point, reviewed once, with no count of similar mislabels and no measure of how much capacity they represent. It also says nothing about Siena's actual grid or power conditions. The entry records the determination and stops there.
